text.p: Industrial conglomerate Desc Sociedad de Fomento Industrial SA is expected to report strong 1996 earnings driven by its autoparts and agribusiness subsidiaries, analysts said.

A survey of four analysts predicted an average 6.10 pesos net earnings per share for 1996 as a whole, with estimates ranging from 5.63 pesos to 6.44 pesos. Desc reported 1995 earnings of 1.05 pesos per share.
For Kerry McHugh, an analyst with Goldman Sachs in New York, Desc will be a leading performer in what was a good year for the Mexican conglomerates sector.
"It has been a great year for these companies, with Desc the clear standout," McHugh wrote in a recent report.
Other analysts agreed, pointing to strength in the company's autoparts sector.
"The increase in domestic auto production should help Desc sustain its earlier growth in autoparts sales," said Urban Larson, equity analyst with Salomon Bros. in Mexico City.
"Figures should be pretty good, with the biggest growth in autoparts and agribusiness," said Robert Hulme, an analyst with the Interacciones brokerage in New York.
Hulme added that Desc's recent purchase of the U.S. based Borg-Warner Automotive Inc plant, which has annual sales of some $100 million, should lift revenues.
Analysts generally agreed a strong fourth quarter for agribusiness sales would help overall figures.
"The agribuiness arm looks very positive," said Daniel Goldstein, of ING Barings in Mexico City, "and should have a great fourth quarter. It's a great cash earner."

There was less consensus on Desc's chemical division. Some analysts noted that chemical prices had dropped recently, while others noted they were stronger for carbon-black, one of Desc's leading products.
Analysts were similarly mixed on the outlook for figures by Desc's real estate division.
"Real estate is improving. The problem there is confidence rather than interest rates," Hulme said.
"As always, real estate sales are difficult to predict, but we believe that fourth quarter real estate sales were minimal," McHugh wrote.
